analysis_review: I should preface this review by saying that I’ve only been playing this game for the past year or so, so whilst there are a considerable number of players who have a legitimate gripe about this game being stuck in early-access Hell, I can’t count myself amongst them, although that being said, I do see their side of things. If you love ghost hunting or just the paranormal in general, this game is for you. And for those that aren’t, don’t worry; it’s a great game to play with friends, especially if you’re looking for something spooky, on the cheaper side, and with great replayability. Recent updates have been… janky to say the least, and there are inconsistencies with the mechanics that do need addressing. However, the team behind it is actively adding new updates/events pretty consistently, so some turbulence is to be expected. The new character model system has been especially devicive, but don’t let that put you off; as long as you’re not expecting in-depth character customization, you should be fine. At the end of the day, for £16, I feel I’ve gotten way more than my money’s worth out of it and will continue to do so. I hope you do too!

analysis_review: Old Phas - 8.5/10 New Phas- 6.5/10 A pioneer in it's genre with many clones released as a result. Was very fun at launch and would easily make you feel uneasy thinking there's ghosts in your house, and is insane in VR, but lost me around 2022. I enjoy watching it on YouTube more than playing it these days. So many different items to learn and way too many ghost types, you have to memorize a textbook and no-life grind it to learn all the traits and you'll likely get your neck snapped 300 times before you get there. 90% of the time you'll get 2 pieces of evidence and just sit there waiting until the 3rd one appears after half the team is already dead. The most recent new animation update isn't too bad and it seems like the economy was improved a bit but I enjoy going back and playing the early versions from SteamDB more. Trolling around in lobbies is more entertaining than the base game, that is, if you can find a lobby that's not a boosting lobby. If you've never played it before you'll probably enjoy it still though.

analysis_review: I used to really love playing this game, but it seems the devs have just been making questionable decisions ever since the item update. Rather than rework maps that no one likes, like school or prison, they reworked a beloved map. I actually like new Tanglewood, but it feels like they only did that because it was much easier to rework than a bigger map. The new update with character customization, which is when I'm writing this, added a load of new weird things I wish didn't make it to live. Using items now feels sluggish and can often be detrimental for survival when the ghost spawns right next to you to hunt. Wanna use incense? Hope you like the 1 second long animation before it gets going. Wanna use T3 salt to slow the ghost? Another 1 second animation. The way a lot of items are held now also bothers me as I can barely read the details some of the items have on their display now. It's so tiny and low resolution due to the distance from the camera that it makes it difficult to actually use stuff like T1 thermometer or even T3 sound recorder. Holding a video camera on a tripod also sucks since the screen on the camera is insanely tiny while holding JUST the camera puts it WAAAAY too close to my screen and I can't see anything but the little screen. The new character animations are broken and look worse than the placeholder ones we had. Someone turns around and the legs break. The arms and wrists look broken when holding most items, etc. To top it all off, they somehow broke dropping items. I've essentially gotten softlocked almost every job since the update since dropping an item is a gamble on whether or not it falls through the map. Goodbye perfect hunts. There's also still the bug of getting 3 evidence for one ghost, but it's a completely different ghost, and no, I'm not talking about a mimic. I mean getting 3 evidence for a wraith, but it somehow ends up being a spirit despite having proof that all the evidence wasn't for spirit. It's a shame because this game was a lot of fun to me, even on solo. It's still fun at its core, but with each new update comes a new issue that actively harms gameplay. I really hope the devs actually fix the bigger problems instead of focusing on small things because they're easier to do.
